title: Contract-test generated storage keys against the central allowlist
symptom: A background media job fails before its provider call because a newly generated object-key shape is rejected by the shared storage guard.
rootCause: The feature added a server-generated storage namespace without extending or contract-testing the central private-key allowlist, while its unit tests replaced the storage service with a permissive mock.
reusableRules: Amends `references/service-implementation.md` under File uploads & ingest: whenever a feature adds a server-generated object-key namespace or shape, use a canonical domain key builder and add a contract test that passes that builder's real output through the central storage-key validator. Keep adjacent wrong-extension, wrong-suffix, traversal, and malformed-identifier cases rejected so extending the allowlist does not widen it accidentally.

evidence.note: Defines the canonical server-generated temporary-frame and generated-video key shapes used by the worker.
Shows the central exact-shape allowlist shared by private-object reads, writes, copies, and deletes.
Exercises the canonical builders against the real validator and proves neighboring malformed shapes remain rejected.

verification: Focused storage, media-handler, and job-runner regression suite passed: 32 tests.
Full API suite passed: 40 suites and 258 tests.
API formatting, targeted lint, TypeScript typecheck, Nest build, and tenant-scope checks passed.
excludedProjectDetails: Removed the product name, provider name, model, bucket, exact feature namespace, and account/balance details.

The existing API skill already requires allowed namespaces, traversal rejection, MIME allowlists, and server-generated final keys; this proposal only refines that rule with builder-to-allowlist contract testing.
